Release Focus: Fix Remaining Chinese/Japanese/Korean Text Leakage With a Two-Layer Language Filter, and Remove Developer-Facing 'Mock' Debug Label From Customer-Facing Output
Description: Addressed continued reports of Chinese characters appearing throughout location names on the generated page (not just in the trip title, which v020 had already fixed) — the user reported that 'location names are all coming out in Chinese' across the day-card locations, map pin labels, and story text, explicitly requesting that only Thai or English ever be shown since Chinese script is unreadable for their customers. Root-caused this as an incomplete v019 fix: requesting only accept-language='th' (a single language) from Nominatim causes it to fall straight through to the OSM object's raw local-script name (e.g. Chinese) whenever that specific place lacks a Thai name tag in OpenStreetMap's database, entirely skipping any English fallback — which turns out to be common for smaller, less-mapped locations such as individual streets or minor attractions in China, even when the containing city itself does have both Thai and English name tags available. Also addressed a second, separate request: asking to 'go ahead and connect' the AI capability referenced by the visible '(Mock — ยังไม่ได้เชื่อม AI จริง)' annotation shown next to story bullets, and what information would be needed to do so.
Key Changes: Verified via Nominatim's own source-level documentation (its Locales class explicitly supporting standard RFC2616 Accept-Language parsing including comma-separated language lists with quality values) that a single-language request is the wrong approach for reliable fallback behavior, and changed the accept-language parameter sent on every reverse-geocoding request from a single 'th' value to 'th,en;q=0.5' — this tells Nominatim to prefer a Thai name tag first, and only if that specific tag doesn't exist for the given OSM object, fall back to an English name tag, before finally giving up and returning the object's untranslated local-script default name; Added a second, independent safety-net layer purely in application code (not dependent on Nominatim's behavior at all): a Unicode-range regex covering CJK Unified Ideographs, CJK Extension A, Hiragana, Katakana, and Hangul Syllables, used to positively detect any remaining unreadable script in a resolved place/district/city/country string; verified against 13 realistic test strings including pure Chinese, pure Japanese (both Kanji and Hiragana/Katakana), Korean Hangul, and several correctly-passing mixed Thai+English and English-only cases; Rebuilt _format_location_display() to run every incoming name field through this detector before composing the final display string, and to actively drop (treat as absent) any field found to still contain unreadable script rather than including it — meaning the composition logic gracefully falls through to progressively broader fields (specific place → district → city → country → raw GPS coordinates as the final fallback) exactly as it already did for genuinely-missing data, now also triggered by data that is present but unreadable; verified this correctly and specifically drops only the untranslatable field while preserving other genuinely-clean fields in the same response (e.g. a Chinese street name is dropped while a Thai/English city name in the very same API response is retained), producing a more informative result than a blanket coordinate fallback would; Additionally applied this same cleaning at the point the city name is first cached from each geocoding call, ensuring the already-clean city value flows correctly into the separately-existing v020 city-level trip-title and day-area logic without needing any further changes there; Rigorously distinguished between testing this fix correctly (by mocking only the outbound network request layer, allowing the real, unmodified cleaning logic under test to execute exactly as it would in production) versus an initial flawed test attempt that mistakenly replaced the entire geocoding function itself and thus bypassed the very logic meant to be verified — corrected this and confirmed, scanning the complete generated HTML output character-by-character for the full Unicode ranges covered by the filter, that zero Chinese, Japanese, or Korean characters remain anywhere on the page for a realistic reproduction of the reported Kunming-Dali trip scenario; Separately, rewrote the Mock-mode (no-AI) narrative fallback text to remove the developer-facing '(Mock — ยังไม่ได้เชื่อม AI จริง)' annotation that had been appearing directly on the customer-facing, shareable Travel Passport webpage — this technical, debug-style phrasing was never meant to be seen by end customers viewing a finished, shared travel page, mirroring the same reasoning already applied to the AI-written badge removed in v018; the underlying location/time bullet-point content itself is preserved unchanged, only the parenthetical developer note is removed, and the Streamlit-side status messages shown to the app's creator (not the customer-facing page) continue to clearly indicate whether AI was used, attempted-and-failed, or not enabled at all; Directly answered the user's question about how to actually connect a real AI provider by substantially rewriting and reordering the in-app '🤖 เชื่อมต่อ AI' guidance section to lead with a concrete numbered three-step walkthrough (enable the checkbox and pick a provider, obtain a free Google AI Studio API key in under a minute with no billing setup required, paste it in and click Generate) explicitly confirming that no additional data beyond what is already collected elsewhere in the form is required, and reordered the provider radio buttons to present the free, no-credit-card Gemini option as the default, recommended first choice rather than Claude; Re-ran the complete v009/v010/v017/v018/v019/v020 regression suite confirming all prior fixes remain fully intact, and verified the complete generated HTML/CSS/JavaScript remains well-formed and syntactically valid after these changes
